item.title: Three Threat Groups Target Russian Enterprises With Backdoors, Ransomware, and Wipers
item.description:
Enterprises in Russia have emerged as the target of three threat activity clusters tracked as NightEagle, Hacking Cat, and Toy Ghouls, according to multiple reports from Kaspersky.
The cybersecurity vendor said it has identified attacks mounted by NightEagle (aka APT-Q-95), a threat actor known to be active since at least 2023, that involve new techniques for persistence and lateral movement.

item.title: Parallels Desktop Flaw Lets Non-Admin Mac Users Gain Root, but Intel Macs Can't Install Fix
item.description:

item.title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
item.description:
Google has disclosed that a high-severity security flaw in its Pixel Cellular Modem has come under exploitation in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58704 (CVSS score: 8.0), is a privilege escalation flaw.

item.title: Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap
item.description: A leaked credential shows up in a criminal marketplace, or a vulnerability gets a disclosure advisory, and either one can be weaponized against a real target before most security teams have triaged the alert. Attackers are combining that kind of intelligence with AI-assisted exploitation to accelerate the path from exposure to breach faster than most security programs are built to react.
